chapters.nameEn: Baudhayana: The Pythagorean Theorem & Square Root of 2
chapters.overview: Contains the earliest explicit statement of the Pythagorean theorem for the diagonal of a rectangle, and highly precise rational approximations for √2 used in Vedic altar construction.

slokas.deva: दीर्घचतुरस्रस्याक्ष्णया रज्जु: पार्श्वमानी तिर्यग्मानी च यत् पृथग्भूते कुरुतस्तदुभयं करोति ॥
slokas.translit: dīrghacaturasrasyākṣṇayā rajjuḥ pārśvamānī tiryagmānī ca yat pṛthagbhūte kurutastadubhayaṃ karoti ||
slokas.translation: The diagonal rope of a rectangle produces both which the flank and the horizontal side produce separately. (c² = a² + b²)

slokas.deva: समस्य द्विकरणी। प्रमाणं तृतीयेन वर्धयेत्तच्च चतुर्थेनात्मचतुस्त्रिंशोनेन सविशेषः।
slokas.translit: samasya dvikaraṇī. pramāṇaṃ tṛtīyena vardhayettacca caturthenātmacatustriṃśonena saviśeṣaḥ.
slokas.translation: The measure (diagonal of a square) is increased by its third, and this third by its fourth, diminished by the thirty-fourth part of that fourth. (Approximation of √2)

formula.title: Baudhayana's Approximation for Root 2
formula.notes: Accurate to 5 decimal places. Used to construct perfectly scaled Agnicayana altars.
